name: e⁺e⁻ → μ⁺μ⁻
explanation: An electron and positron annihilate into a virtual photon, which converts into a muon–antimuon pair. At higher energies the Z boson also contributes through the same diagram topology.

name: e⁻e⁻ → e⁻e⁻ (Møller scattering)
explanation: Two electrons repel by exchanging a virtual photon, a purely electromagnetic t-channel process. Each electron line keeps its identity because electron number is conserved along each fermion line.

name: e⁻μ⁻ → e⁻μ⁻
explanation: An electron scatters off a muon by exchanging a virtual photon. The electron and muon lines never mix, because electron and muon lepton numbers are separately conserved.

name: e⁺e⁻ → e⁺e⁻ (Bhabha, s-channel)
explanation: An electron and positron annihilate into a virtual photon that re-creates an e⁺e⁻ pair. The full Bhabha cross-section also needs a t-channel diagram, because the final state matches the initial one.

name: Compton scattering e⁻γ → e⁻γ
explanation: A photon scatters off an electron: the electron absorbs the photon, becoming a virtual electron, then emits a new photon. The internal line must again be an electron to conserve charge and lepton number.

name: e⁺e⁻ → γγ
explanation: An electron and positron annihilate into two photons through a virtual electron exchanged between the two vertices. Two photons are needed because a single photon cannot conserve both energy and momentum.

name: γγ → e⁺e⁻
explanation: Two photons collide and create an electron–positron pair, converting light into matter. A virtual electron links the two photon vertices.

name: Electron self-energy
explanation: An electron emits a virtual photon and reabsorbs it, forming a loop that corrects the electron propagator. Such loops are the origin of mass renormalization in QED.

name: QED vertex correction
explanation: A virtual photon is emitted and reabsorbed by the electron around its interaction with an external photon. This one-loop diagram gives the leading correction to the electron's magnetic moment, the anomalous g-2.

name: Vacuum polarization
explanation: A photon briefly fluctuates into a virtual fermion–antifermion pair and then recombines. This loop screens electric charge and makes the electromagnetic coupling run with energy.
